newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombian stocks end mixed amid demand for bank.
newsitem.headline: Colombian stocks end mixed amid demand for bank.

text.p: BOGOTA, May 2 Reuter - Colombian stocks ended mixed in sessions dominated by cross deals in Banco de Bogota.
Bogota's .IBB index dipped 0.82 percent to 1,138.96 amid an 11 billion peso volume while Medellin's IBOMED .IBMG general price index edged up 0.34 percent to 17,457.98 amid a 1.9 billion peso volume.
"The market was mixed because there's expectation about a possible fall in interest rates especially in view of the trend in inflation," one Bogota broker said.
The National Statistics Department said Friday that the rise in the April consumer price index was 1.62 percent, the smallest April gain in 19 years.

More than 80 percent of the volume on the Bogota exchange was made up of Banco de Bogota shares -- flagship of Luis Carlos Sarmiento's financial empire. The share fell 10 percent to 5,847 in a pocket-to-pocket cross-deal involving 1.1 million of the total 1.6 million shares traded Friday.
In Medellin, however, the bank gained 1.06 percent to 6,570.01 on the back of high hopes for good first-quarter results.

There was also heavy demand for companies of the powerful Sindicato Antioqueno conglomerate. Cement manufacturer Cemento Argos ARG.BG. was up 0.94 percent to 8,783 in Bogota and up 1 percent to 8,800 in Medellin.
Insurance company Suramericana de Seguros, head of the Sindicato, was unchanged at 26,540 in Bogota and up 0.8 percent to 26,550 in Medellin as foreign funds stepped in to buy.

Cigarette manufacturer Coltabaco gained 0.92 percent to close at 3,280 in Medellin and cement manufacturer Cementos del Caribe was up 0.98 percent to 5,655, also in Medellin. Both are part of the Sindicato Antioqueno.
